look_here_first: KNOTROOT BRISTLEGRASS (Setaria parviflora): Start at the PERENNIAL BASE. The new real source photo shows short knotty rhizomes and buds, a reliable contrast with many annual foxtails. Next peel back an attached leaf to see the TRUE fringe-of-hairs ligule (about 0.4–1.2 mm in Kew). Examine a dense uniform foxtail panicle, then ONE spikelet with its 4–12 persistent bristles attached below it, NOT the purple feathery flowering stigmas. The new photographed 3-mm montage labels lower and upper GLUMES and LEMMAS; these are real botanical parts. Source collection is Croatia, and a matched Texas voucher remains pending.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Distinguish from annual yellow foxtail S. pumila and green foxtail S. viridis using actual knotty perennial rhizomes; neither is a canonical species here. S. reverchonii has longer interrupted heads with bristles much sparser, S. scheelei has usually one very long conspicuous projecting bristle and longer loose/tapered head. Foxtail millet S. italica is cultivated/escaped annual; its dense head alone is insufficient.
diagnostic_sequence: Inspect the basal rootstock for short hard knotty rhizomes; do not uproot protected or sensitive plants.
Use a hand lens on spikelets: several bristles at each base; spikelets approximately 2–3 mm.
Photograph leaf ligule and a complete plant habit; existing single macro does not show the decisive rhizome.
not_reliable_alone: Color or texture of seedhead without bristle group macro
Bristles mistaken for true floret awns or flower stigmas
Mature spikelet counts read from a photo too small to show attachment
Cultivated or habitat context presented as confirmed local nativity

best_field_traits: KNOTROOT BRISTLEGRASS (perennial): FIRST verify a living short hard knotty basal rhizome, then a generally short even-width dense foxtail head (~3–8 cm). FNA reports 4–12 persistent bristles, 2–12 mm long, beneath each spikelet; they must be counted from a genuinely intact head at 10–20×. Our only stored macro shows green bracts and pink emergent floral tissue with a 2-mm scale, NOT the perennial rhizome or a countable group of 4–12 basal bristles.
Perennial with firm short knotty rhizomes, to about 4 cm in a local Texas botanical treatment, sometimes with swollen buds at shoot bases.
Stem nodes often bent (geniculate); short densely bristly cylindrical flowering heads commonly 25–70 mm.
Many sterile bristles grouped beneath each spikelet: usually six or seven, observed local-treatment range about four to twelve.
Spikelets about 2.2–2.5 mm long; no floret awns (bristles are sterile reduced branchlets).
A true FRINGE-OF-HAIRS ligule about 0.4–1.2 mm (Kew/GrassBase) at blade/sheath junction; do not teach an obvious tall membranous flap. Source S. parviflora sl16 provides an actual ligule photograph.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Complete short densely bristly terminal head with ruler and multiple intact spikelet bases
Rooted same-plant hard knotty rhizomes with buds and centimeter ruler (only where collection legal)
True 4–12 basal persistent bristles clearly separable from exserted flower parts (10–20×)
Intact 2–2.8 mm ripe spikelet, glumes/upper lemma, and hair-like ligule
crew_field_check: First find the WHOLE panicle and compare crowded/loose head arrangement without forcing species from silhouette.
Inspect an intact attached SPIKELET at 10–20×. Count the SUBTENDING PERSISTENT BRISTLES (sterile branches), not grass awns or protruding flower parts.
Record bristle count/length and spikelet length using a 1-mm scale, and compare the same-plant collar ligule.
Check a rooted base only where collecting is legal: annual fibrous millet vs knotty rhizomatous perennial parviflora/reverchonii, and perennial scheelei.
Existing archival images do not prove every underlying bristle count or rhizome; if unresolved identify Setaria sp.
detailed_photo_learning_sequence_2026102: 1. First show actual fully photographed rooted perennial bunch and separate flowering culms (Commons sl1).
2. Show a source-identified short nodular RHIZOME and swollen shoot bud beside fine roots; original sl13 includes 10-mm bar. Don't mistake a fibrous root for a rhizome.
3. Follow lower sheath to true blade junction; sl16 shows a ligule fringe OF HAIRS, about 0.4–1.2 mm in Kew. Do not infer an unphotographed membrane.
4. Look at the whole narrow even-width fuzzy head (not only a single bristle), then choose one identifiable mature spikelet (original sl26).
5. On 3-mm closeup sl24, locate sterile PERSISTENT BRISTLES subtending green spikelet, and purple feathery STIGMAS emerging from flowering tissue. Count bristles belonging to one attached spikelet.
6. Examine measured sl29 multi-angle spikelet series: identify original author labels Glu' and Glu'' for glumes and Lem' and Lem'' for lemmas; no fake arrows.
7. Compare other-species S. reverchonii and S. scheelei photo panels by head spacing/bristle layout, then distinguish annual alien foxtails via the RHIZOME on a locally rooted sample.
8. Crew teach-back: separate rhizome/root, hair ligule, bristle/stigma, and glume/lemma on the photographed real plant parts before a confirmed ID.

items.why_it_matters: FOXTAIL MILLET (INTRODUCED annual crop/escape): start with stout annual culms, broad foliage, and a heavy dense often lobed or nodding foxtail head. Flora of North America usually describes 1–3 persistent subtending bristles (to ~12 mm), NOT 'numerous bristles beneath every spikelet'. A crop-derived head varies greatly; distinguish from perennial native bristlegrasses using rooted duration, panicle shape and ripe spikelets.

Unlike Reverchon's shorter sparse bristles, these long bristles are actually obvious in the saved flowering photograph. Edwards Plateau shady limestone canyon habitat is supportive, not conclusive.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Knotroot bristlegrass — rhizome, collar, real bristle origin, and spikelet parts
steps: Start with the locally archived living plant and follow one entire slender foxtail head down to its leafy basal tuft. Then open the separate actual excavated knotty rhizome photo; it shows the connected hard underground stem and attached roots that the live field shot does NOT expose.

Open the locally stored photographer-identified leaf collar photograph and find the true short hair-fringe ligule; do not infer an unmeasured fringe length or confuse scattered sheath hairs with the ligule.
Check the original close-up with 2-mm scale: purple feathery protrusions are STIGMAS. They are reproductive flower organs, not the persistent SETARIA bristles.

Compare the original sl24 source photo, which the photographer labels 'spikelet with bristles at the base': follow several stiff bristles back to their subtending base, do not label an awn or a purple stigma as a bristle. The sl24 local archive was subsequently byte-verified in GitHub; exact bristle insertion/count on a Texas specimen remains unverified.

Use the source-labelled sl29 dissected glume/lemma plate: separate lower glume (Glu'), upper glume (Glu''), lower lemma (Lem') and upper fertile lemma (Lem''). Source labels are original author evidence, not newly invented arrow endpoints.

Compare annual green/yellow foxtails and foxtail millet against an ACTUAL rooted rhizomatous Setaria parviflora plant. S. reverchonii and S. scheelei differ in panicle/bristle architecture; number and length vary and must be counted on intact attached spikelets.

Keep taxon identity provisional for the Croatian source series as to Texas locality. Completion still needs same-voucher Texas root, collar and multiple measured ripe spikelets with naturally attached subtending bristles.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Avoid native/introduced calls or true species ID solely from bristle silhouette. Count several attached mature spikelets and study rootstock on the same plant.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Five exact-species public-safe images physically archived (one sl26 spikelet, sl13 rhizome, sl16 ligule, sl24 bristle macro, sl29 glume-lemma montage). 2 new macro JPEGs independently read back and source licenses CC BY-SA 4.0 verified 2026-10-24. Two new gross markers target actual visible bristle SHAFT and purple stigma in sl24, not an invisible bristle insertion. Croatian photos do NOT certify Hays identity; same-voucher mature count and mobile QA missing. 2026-10-26: source CC BY-SA 4.0 whole-plant image sl1 is now a locally archived EXIF-free JPEG, with three gross-only arrow markers; original NC-licensed S. scheelei comparison remains preserved with attribution, subject to noncommercial use and individual license recheck. Site must pass rights-filtered deployment before live claim.

what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Complete short densely bristly terminal head with ruler and multiple intact spikelet bases
Rooted same-plant hard knotty rhizomes with buds and centimeter ruler (only where collection legal)
True 4–12 basal persistent bristles clearly separable from exserted flower parts (10–20×)
Intact 2–2.8 mm ripe spikelet, glumes/upper lemma, and hair-like ligule

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · ROOTED KNOTROOT AND EVEN FOXTAIL
field_id_short_tiles.short: LOOK HERE FIRST: a short, hard, knotty perennial rhizome beneath a dense, nearly even-width foxtail head
field_id_short_tiles.details: Perennial rhizomatous grass with culms roughly 30–120 cm and a compact cylindrical panicle typically 3–8(10) cm (FNA). Inspect an attached rootstock before treating this as an annual foxtail. Existing source-labelled Croatian rhizome and habit photos teach the organs, but do not certify a Hays County voucher.
field_id_short_tiles.status: GROWTH FORM TAUGHT — SAME-VOUCHER TEXAS PLANT NEEDED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · TRUE HAIR-FRINGE LIGULE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Open the inner blade–sheath junction; ligule is a short fringe of hairs, not an erect membrane
field_id_short_tiles.details: FNA reports the true ligule <1 mm; Kew/GrassBase reports about 0.4–1.2 mm. Leaf blades often 2–8 mm wide. The source-labelled sl16 photo shows collar placement but cannot establish a measured Texas ligule. Do not point to purple stigmas or sheath-mouth hairs as the ligule.
field_id_short_tiles.status: TRUE COLLAR SOURCE PHOTO — CALIBRATED LOCAL MACRO NEEDED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · COUNT BRISTLES BELOW A SPIKELET
field_id_short_tiles.short: Usually 4–12 persistent bristles, about 2–12 mm, BELOW each spikelet; these are sterile branchlets, not awns
field_id_short_tiles.details: At 10–20× trace bristles to the individual spikelet's short basal branch; count several mature units. FNA gives 4–12 and 2–12 mm, while the local Williamson County treatment commonly finds 6–7 (range 4–12), about 1.3–7.5 mm. Pink feathery stigmas are flower parts, NOT bristles. The archived sl24 macro shows shafts but not a Texas same-voucher attachment count.
field_id_short_tiles.status: ARCHIVED BRISTLE PHOTO — ATTACHMENT COUNT UNMEASURED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · OPEN BOTH GLUMES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Mature spikelets ~2–2.8 mm; lower glume short and 3-veined, upper glume longer and commonly 5-veined
field_id_short_tiles.details: FNA describes lower glume ~one-third and upper ~one-half to two-thirds of spikelet length; the local Texas treatment instead gives lower glume 1.1–1.5 mm and upper 1.7–1.8 mm on 2.2–2.5 mm spikelets. Published proportions differ: never enforce one ratio without a measured mature specimen. The source-labelled sl29 montage shows Glu' and Glu''; its original labels do not replace same-plant verification.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · TWO FLORETS, NO LEMMA AWNS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Lower sterile or staminate floret plus a hardened, transversely wrinkled upper fertile lemma
field_id_short_tiles.details: Lower sterile lemma approximately spikelet length and generally 5-veined; upper fertile lemma about 2–2.6 mm (Kew) with conspicuous transverse ridges. Open a ripe spikelet to see both lemmas and paleas separately. No true long lemma awn: the persistent basal bristles belong to sterile panicle branchlets. Do not invent fine arrows where the archived pixels cannot resolve an organ.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL LABELLED REPRODUCTIVE MONTAGE — CALIBRATED DISSECTION NEEDED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · CHECK THE LOCAL FOXTAIL LOOK-ALIKES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Perennial knotty rhizome and many bristles separate it from annual foxtails and the other native Setaria
field_id_short_tiles.details: S. italica is an introduced annual with a heavy often lobed head and usually fewer bristles; S. reverchonii has a slender often interrupted head with sparse 2–8 mm bristles where present; S. scheelei often has one very long 10–35 mm projecting bristle. S. pumila and S. viridis are annual look-alikes, not installed canonical genus species. Use actual roots, attached mature spikelets and the true ligule; do not infer local nativity from Croatian images.
field_id_short_tiles.status: FIELD COMPARISON — MATCHED TEXAS VOUCHERS NEEDED

NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO: Same documented Hays-area specimen: rooted knotty rhizome connected to the flowering culm, 10-mm rootstock and cm whole-plant scales.
Opened true hair-fringe ligule with 1-mm scale, both collar and sheath margins, from the same local specimen.
Three attached ripe 2–2.8 mm spikelets each with 1-mm scale and clearly traced 4–12 persistent basal bristles; count insertion separately from purple stigmas.
One dissected same-voucher mature spikelet with lower/upper glumes, lower sterile lemma/palea and transversely ridged upper fertile lemma; record conflicting published glume ratios.
NEEDS_SITE_QA: Preserve all six original image records, CC BY-SA 4.0 author/source/ShareAlike terms, existing arrows, Croatian origin and taxonomic holds; check which JPEGs are physically archived versus remote.
Check sl24 purple stigma versus actual bristle shaft annotations and sl29 original Glu/Lem labels at actual pixel resolution; no unsupported insertion or microvenation arrows.
Verify ordinary public species gallery renders each licensed image and original credits, then inspect mobile overlays; no Pages action performed in this lane.
Retain FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS until a local matched specimen, measured mature reproductive/collar anatomy, valid public rights and site QA are all verified.
grass_finalization.public_ready_criteria: Require species-authenticated local same-voucher growth/collar and ripe reproductive photographs with actual measurements, anatomy arrows only on resolved pixels, individual image rights and attribution, and verified public/mobile gallery before marking FINISHED. Preserve taxonomy and native-range holds.
grass_finalization.notes: Existing canonical species only. Published measurements are reference ranges, not measured from existing JPEG pixels. No images, annotations, genus/family modules or website files changed.
